title: JAMB UTME (Use of English, Mathematics, Science)

exam.scoring: UTME aggregate out of 400 (English 60 Q/90 min; other subjects 40 Q/60 min)

content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the JAMB official syllabus: Use of English paper (60 questions) plus 40-question subject papers covering Mathematics and General Science. Not a capture of past exam questions.

items.stem: The village headman summoned the youths to the square and told them that the stream which had served their grandparents had begun to dry, and that unless they acted the farms would fail. Why did the headman call the meeting?
options: To warn that the drying stream threatened the farms
To celebrate a good harvest with the youths
To plan a journey to a distant market
To accuse the youths of stealing water
items.explanation: The headman explains that the stream is drying and the farms will fail unless action is taken, so his concern is the threat to the farms. The other options are not mentioned in the passage.

items.stem: When the letter arrived, Adaeze read it twice and her hands trembled as she unfolded the paper. The word trembled as used here suggests that Adaeze was feeling
items.explanation: Trembling hands while unfolding awaited news suggests nervous anxiety mixed with eagerness, not anger, tiredness or amusement.

items.stem: The teacher told the class that success would depend less on luck than on steady revision and that those who crammed the night before often forgot what they had learnt. What lesson is the teacher teaching?
options: Examinations should be avoided by students
Students should not sleep before an examination
Steady revision is more useful than last-minute cramming
Luck decides the result of every examination
items.explanation: The teacher contrasts luck with steady revision and warns against cramming, so the lesson is that consistent revision works better than last-minute study.

items.stem: Although the bridge had been declared safe, many villagers still avoided it because they remembered the flood that had carried away the old one. What does the passage reveal about the villagers?
options: They cannot read the safety certificate
They built the bridge with their own hands
They prefer to walk long distances for exercise
Their fear comes from past experience rather than present danger
items.explanation: The villagers avoid the new bridge not because it is unsafe but because the memory of the flood that destroyed the old bridge still frightens them.

items.stem: Mama Nkechi called out the prices of her tomatoes in a market full of noise, and buyers moved toward her stall as if drawn by a magnet. What does the comparison to a magnet suggest?
options: Her stall was built of iron
The market was about to close
items.explanation: A magnet pulls metal strongly, so the simile shows how powerfully her voice drew customers to her stall.

items.stem: Emeka was praised for returning a wallet he found on the road. Although his friends laughed at him, the owner of the wallet blessed him and gave him a small reward. What quality did Emeka display?
items.explanation: Returning found property to its owner is an act of honesty, which the owner acknowledged with a blessing and a reward.

items.stem: The rain fell without pause for three days, the river swelled, and the farmers watched their young maize bend and drown. What is the effect of the rain described in the passage?
options: The drying up of the river
Destruction of the crops on the farms
A rich harvest for the farmers
items.explanation: The swollen river drowns the young maize, so the rain destroys the crops rather than helping them; the other options contradict the passage.

items.stem: She spoke quietly, yet when she finished no one argued because her argument had answered every objection before it was raised. What does the passage say about her speech?
items.explanation: The speech silenced all argument because it had already answered every objection, showing that it was persuasive and complete.

items.stem: The old man said his garden fed his body while his books fed his mind, and he refused to neglect either. What does this comparison imply?
options: He valued both physical and mental nourishment
He had no time for books at all
He sold vegetables to earn a living
items.explanation: Gardening feeding the body and books feeding the mind shows that he valued both physical and mental development equally.

items.stem: The team lost the first match but won the next five, and their coach said the early defeat had taught them more than any victory could. What does the coach mean?
options: The coach wanted them to lose on purpose
They learnt valuable lessons from losing
They were simply lucky to win
The first match did not matter at all
items.explanation: The coach says the defeat taught them more than a victory would, meaning they gained useful lessons from the loss that helped them improve.

items.stem: Visitors often mistook the quiet librarian for a stern woman, yet the children who came for stories knew the warmth behind her silence. What does the passage show about the librarian?
options: She was as unkind as she looked
Her quiet manner hid a kind nature
items.explanation: The children who knew her saw warmth behind her silence, so her quiet manner concealed a kind and gentle nature.

items.stem: The trader counted his coins twice before handing them over and said that a man who cannot count his money will soon have none to count. What does the saying advise?
options: Spending money as quickly as possible
items.explanation: Counting money carefully and the warning about losing it both counsel prudence and careful management of money.

items.stem: Some climbers turned back because the peak seemed too far, but those who continued found that the view from the top repaid every step. What does the passage suggest about perseverance?
options: It brings rewards that quitting cannot
It is always easy and painless
It should be avoided by everyone
items.explanation: Those who persevered reached the top and were rewarded with the view, while those who quit never received it, so perseverance pays.

items.stem: The remarks of the chairman were brief but poignant, and many in the hall wiped their eyes as he described the sacrifices of the late founder. The word poignant most nearly means
items.explanation: People wiping their eyes shows the remarks touched them deeply, so poignant means deeply moving or emotionally stirring.

items.stem: Although he was the youngest in the group, he was chosen to lead because he listened more than he spoke and acted only after weighing the facts. Why was he chosen as leader?
options: Because he talked more than anyone
Because he was the oldest member
Because he was thoughtful and attentive
Because he was the tallest person
items.explanation: He was chosen for listening carefully and weighing facts before acting, which shows thoughtfulness and attentiveness rather than age or height.

items.stem: After the flood the family returned to find their home still standing although the roof had been torn away, and their neighbours helped them rebuild before the next rains. What does this show about the neighbours?
options: They wanted to take the house
items.explanation: Helping the family rebuild before the next rains shows generosity and support, not indifference or bad intentions.

items.stem: The drum began slowly, then quickened until the dancers could hardly keep pace, and when it stopped the people waited breathlessly for it to begin again. What does this description convey?
options: The rhythm of the drum held the crowd spellbound
The dancers were tired and went home
The drum was broken and useless
The crowd was leaving the square
items.explanation: Waiting breathlessly for the drum to start again shows the crowd was captivated, so the rhythm held them spellbound.

items.stem: He did not boast of his wealth but built a well for the village and paid the school fees of ten children, saying that a full barn is useless if the village is hungry. What does this reveal about him?
options: He wanted only praise from others
items.explanation: Building a well and paying school fees shows generosity and concern for the community, which contradicts greed or a desire for praise.

items.stem: The two brothers shared a room, a bed and even their clothes, and when one fell ill the other sat by him all night without sleeping. What does this behaviour reveal?
options: A deep fear of the dark
items.explanation: Sharing everything and keeping a night vigil by a sick brother reveals deep care and devotion.

items.stem: As the candidates waited in the hall, some read their notes for the last time, others stared at the ceiling, and a few prayed quietly until the invigilator entered. What mood does the passage create?
items.explanation: Reading notes, staring at the ceiling and praying while waiting for the invigilator create the tense, nervous mood of examination anticipation.

items.stem: The new road cut the journey from six hours to two, so farmers could send their produce to the city before it spoilt and traders came more often. What is the main benefit described?
options: Faster transport improved trade and reduced waste
The city moved closer to the village
items.explanation: Shorter travel time let farmers sell produce before it spoilt and brought more traders, so faster transport improved trade and reduced waste.

items.stem: She failed once, sat the examination again and passed with distinction, proving that a fall is not the end of the race. What is the message of the passage?
options: A person should never try again
Failure can be overcome through persistence
items.explanation: She failed, tried again and passed with distinction, showing that persistence can turn failure into success.

items.stem: The elders often quoted the proverb that a child who washes his hands clean may eat with kings whenever they reminded the young ones to be honest and diligent. What does the proverb mean?
options: Washing the hands always causes hunger
Children should avoid the company of elders
Good character earns respect and opportunity
Kings enjoy eating with young children
items.explanation: The proverb is quoted to urge honesty and diligence, and it means that good character earns respect and opens doors to opportunity.

items.stem: Which word is nearest in meaning to reluctant as used in the sentence, The manager was reluctant to approve the request?
items.explanation: Reluctant means unwilling or hesitant, so it is nearest in meaning to unwilling; eager and pleased are its opposites.

items.stem: Choose the word that is nearest in meaning to abandon as used in the sentence, The villagers had to abandon their homes.
items.explanation: To abandon a place is to leave it completely, so desert is the nearest synonym; occupy and rent mean close to the opposite.

items.stem: Choose the word that is nearest in meaning to candid in the sentence, She gave a candid account of the incident.
items.explanation: Candid means honest and straightforward, so frank is the nearest synonym; vague means unclear, which is the opposite.

items.stem: Choose the word that is most nearly opposite in meaning to ancient in the sentence, They studied the ancient ruins.
items.explanation: Ancient means very old, so its opposite is modern; old, historic and famous are not opposites.

items.stem: Choose the word that is most nearly opposite in meaning to frugal in the sentence, She led a frugal life.
items.explanation: Frugal means economical or thrifty, so its opposite is extravagant; careful and thrifty are close in meaning to frugal.

items.stem: Which word is nearest in meaning to verbose as used in the sentence, His verbose speech tired the audience?
items.explanation: Verbose means using more words than necessary, so wordy is the nearest synonym; brief is its opposite.

items.stem: Choose the word that is nearest in meaning to adversity in the sentence, He remained cheerful in adversity.
items.explanation: Adversity means difficulty or misfortune, so hardship is the nearest synonym; comfort, wealth and pleasure are opposites.

items.stem: Fill the gap. Neither the teacher nor the students ____ present at the assembly.
items.explanation: With neither and nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, students, which is plural, so the correct form is were.

items.stem: Fill the gap. The committee has submitted ____ final report to the principal.
items.explanation: The committee is treated as a single body here, so the singular possessive its is correct; their would need a plural subject.

items.stem: Fill the gap. If I ____ you, I would accept the offer without hesitation.
items.explanation: The second conditional uses were for every subject, giving If I were you, which is the standard subjunctive form.

items.stem: Fill the gap. She is the ____ of the two sisters.
items.explanation: When comparing exactly two people the comparative taller is used, not the superlative tallest, which needs three or more.

items.stem: Fill the gap. We arrived ____ the airport long before dawn.
items.explanation: We use at with points and small places such as an airport; in is used for large areas and on is used for surfaces.

items.stem: Fill the gap. He has been living in this town ____ 2010.
items.explanation: Since is used with a point in time from which an action started, while for is used with a period of time such as ten years.

items.stem: Fill the gap. The three girls shared the oranges ____ themselves.
items.explanation: Among is used for sharing between more than two people, while between is used for exactly two.

items.stem: Choose the emphatic form that correctly completes the sentence. It was ____ that broke the window yesterday.
items.explanation: In the emphatic structure introduced by It was, the word that follows takes the subject form he, not the object form him.

items.stem: Choose the option that correctly completes the emphatic sentence. Not only ____ the first prize, but he also set a new record.
items.explanation: When not only begins a sentence the auxiliary comes before the subject, so we write did he win.

items.stem: In the expression to bury the hatchet, the speaker means to
options: hide a weapon in the ground
make peace and end a quarrel
items.explanation: To bury the hatchet is an idiom meaning to stop fighting and make peace, not a literal act of burying a tool.

items.stem: A couch potato is a person who
options: spends much time sitting and watching television
sleeps on a sofa all day
items.explanation: A couch potato is an informal idiom for someone who is inactive and spends much time sitting, especially watching television.

items.stem: To let the cat out of the bag means to
options: release a pet from a bag
buy a cat from a market
items.explanation: To let the cat out of the bag means to disclose a secret, usually accidentally, not to free an animal.

items.stem: The proverb a stitch in time saves nine advises one to
options: wait patiently for problems to pass
act promptly to prevent a bigger problem
items.explanation: The proverb means that dealing with a small problem at once prevents it from growing into a much larger one later.

items.stem: Choose the word that is nearest in meaning to placid in the sentence, The lake was placid that morning.
items.explanation: Placid means calm and peaceful, so it is nearest in meaning to calm; rough is its opposite.

items.stem: Choose the word that is most nearly opposite in meaning to scarce in the sentence, Water became scarce in the dry season.
items.explanation: Scarce means in short supply, so its opposite is abundant; rare and little are close in meaning to scarce.

items.stem: Which of the following words has its primary stress on the SECOND syllable?
items.explanation: Begin is stressed on the second syllable, beGIN, while table, father and market are all stressed on the first syllable.

items.stem: Which of the following words has its primary stress on the FIRST syllable?
items.explanation: Doctor is stressed on the first syllable, DOCtor, whereas police, machine and hotel are stressed on the second.

items.stem: Which of the following words contains a vowel sound different from the others?
items.explanation: Sit, hit and bit all contain the short vowel sound heard in sit, while seat contains the long vowel sound heard in see.

items.stem: Which of the following words contains a vowel sound different from the others?
items.explanation: Cat, hat and mat share the short a sound heard in cat, while cart contains the long a sound heard in car.

items.stem: Which of the following words begins with a consonant sound different from the others?
items.explanation: Chair, church and chief begin with the ch sound heard in chair, while chemist begins with the k sound heard in kite.

items.stem: Which of the following words contains a silent letter?
items.explanation: In comb the letter b is not pronounced, so it is silent; lamp, hand and tent have no silent letters.

items.stem: Which of the following words has its primary stress on the SECOND syllable?
items.explanation: About is stressed on the second syllable, aBOUT, while doctor, mother and letter are stressed on the first.

items.stem: Which of the following words has its primary stress on the FIRST syllable?
items.explanation: Famous is stressed on the first syllable, FA-mous, while decide, begin and enjoy are stressed on the second.

items.stem: Which of the following words ends with a consonant sound different from the others?
items.explanation: Laughed, talked and walked end with the t sound in these past-tense forms, while wanted ends with the id sound heard in wanted.

items.stem: Which of the following words contains a vowel sound different from the others?
items.explanation: Book, cook and look contain the short vowel sound heard in put, while boot contains the long vowel sound heard in food.

items.stem: Which of the following words begins with a consonant sound different from the others?
items.explanation: Knight, knee and know begin with the n sound because the k is silent, while kind begins with the k sound heard in kite.

items.stem: Which of the following words has its primary stress on the SECOND syllable?
items.explanation: Machine is stressed on the second syllable, maCHINE, while village, brother and sister are stressed on the first.

items.stem: Which of the following words has its primary stress on the FIRST syllable?
items.explanation: Teacher is stressed on the first syllable, TEACH-er, while allow, oppose and agree are stressed on the second.

items.stem: Which of the following words ends with a consonant sound different from the others?
items.explanation: Dogs, bags and pens end with the z sound, while cats ends with the s sound heard in cats.

items.stem: Which of the following words contains a vowel sound different from the others?
items.explanation: Bought, caught and taught contain the aw vowel sound heard in law, while doubt contains the ow sound heard in cow.

items.stem: If 2x + 5 = 17, what is the value of x?
items.explanation: Solving gives 2x = 17 - 5 = 12, so x = 12 divided by 2 = 6. Substituting 6 back gives 12 + 5 = 17.

items.stem: Find the roots of the quadratic equation x^2 - 7x + 12 = 0.
items.explanation: Factorising gives (x - 3)(x - 4) = 0, so the roots are x = 3 and x = 4, since 3 times 4 = 12 and 3 + 4 = 7.

items.stem: If x + y = 10 and x - y = 4, what is the value of x?
items.explanation: Adding the two equations gives 2x = 14, so x = 7 and then y = 3. Substituting back, 7 + 3 = 10 and 7 - 3 = 4.

items.stem: Expand the product of the expressions (x + 3) and (x - 2).
items.explanation: Multiplying out gives x^2 - 2x + 3x - 6, which simplifies to x^2 + x - 6.

items.stem: Factorise the expression x^2 - 9 completely.
items.explanation: This is a difference of two squares, so x^2 - 9 = (x - 3)(x + 3). Expanding confirms the middle terms cancel.

items.stem: If 3x - 7 = 2x + 5, what is the value of x?
items.explanation: Subtracting 2x from both sides gives x - 7 = 5, so x = 5 + 7 = 12. Substituting back checks the equality.

items.stem: If 2 raised to the power x equals 32, what is the value of x?
items.explanation: Since 2^5 = 32, the value of x is 5. Writing 32 as 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 confirms the power.

items.stem: Simplify 3^2 multiplied by 3^3, giving the answer as a single number.
items.explanation: When multiplying powers with the same base we add the indices, so 3^2 x 3^3 = 3^5 = 243.

items.stem: Evaluate the logarithm to base 10 of 1000.
items.explanation: Since 10^3 = 1000, the logarithm to base 10 of 1000 equals 3.

items.stem: Simplify the surd expression the square root of 50 plus the square root of 18.
items.explanation: Root 50 = 5 root 2 and root 18 = 3 root 2, so adding gives 5 root 2 + 3 root 2 = 8 root 2.

items.stem: Simplify the expression 6 divided by the square root of 3 in surd form.
items.explanation: Multiplying the numerator and denominator by root 3 gives 6 root 3 divided by 3, which simplifies to 2 root 3.

items.stem: The arithmetic progression 3, 7, 11 continues in the same way. What is its tenth term?
items.explanation: The first term is 3 and the common difference is 4, so the tenth term is 3 + 9 times 4 = 3 + 36 = 39.

items.stem: Find the sum of the first ten terms of the arithmetic progression 2, 4, 6, 8.
items.explanation: With first term 2 and common difference 2, the sum is (10/2)(2 x 2 + 9 x 2) = 5 x 22 = 110.

items.stem: The geometric progression 2, 6, 18 continues in the same way. What is its fifth term?
items.explanation: The common ratio is 3, so the fifth term is 2 times 3^4 = 2 times 81 = 162.

items.stem: Differentiate y = 3x^2 + 2x with respect to x.
items.explanation: The rule for powers multiplies each term by its index and reduces the index by one, giving 6x + 2.

items.stem: Differentiate y = x^3 - 4x with respect to x.
items.explanation: Differentiating term by term gives 3x^2 for x^3 and minus 4 for 4x, so dy/dx = 3x^2 - 4.

items.stem: If y = 5x^2, find the value of dy/dx when x = 2.
items.explanation: Differentiating gives dy/dx = 10x, and substituting x = 2 gives 10 times 2 = 20.

items.stem: Find the indefinite integral of 2x with respect to x.
items.explanation: The integral of 2x is x^2 plus a constant of integration, because differentiating x^2 returns 2x.

items.stem: Find the indefinite integral of the expression 3x^2 + 1 with respect to x.
items.explanation: Integrating term by term gives x^3 for 3x^2 and x for 1, plus the constant, so the result is x^3 + x + C.

items.stem: Evaluate the definite integral of 3x^2 with respect to x from 0 to 2.
items.explanation: The integral of 3x^2 is x^3, and evaluating from 0 to 2 gives 2^3 minus 0^3 = 8.

items.stem: Find the gradient of the curve y = x^2 - 3x + 1 at the point where x = 2.
items.explanation: The gradient is dy/dx = 2x - 3, and substituting x = 2 gives 4 - 3 = 1.

items.stem: Solve the inequality 2x + 3 < 11.
items.explanation: Subtracting 3 from both sides gives 2x < 8, then dividing by 2 gives x < 4.

items.stem: Find the coefficient of x^2 in the expansion of (1 + x)^4.
items.explanation: By the binomial theorem the coefficient is the binomial coefficient 4 choose 2, which equals 6.

items.stem: Two angles of a triangle are 50 degrees and 60 degrees. What is the size of the third angle?
items.explanation: The angles of a triangle sum to 180 degrees, so the third angle is 180 - 50 - 60 = 70 degrees.

items.stem: What is the sum of the interior angles of a quadrilateral?
items.explanation: A quadrilateral can be divided into two triangles, and each triangle has 180 degrees, so the total is 2 times 180 = 360 degrees.

items.stem: Find the area of a triangle whose base is 8 cm and whose height is 5 cm.
items.explanation: The area of a triangle is half the base times the height, so it is 0.5 times 8 times 5 = 20 square cm.

items.stem: Find the area of a circle of radius 7 cm, taking pi as 22 divided by 7.
items.explanation: Area = pi r^2 = (22/7) times 7 times 7 = 22 times 7 = 154 square cm.

items.stem: Find the circumference of a circle of radius 7 cm, taking pi as 22 divided by 7.
items.explanation: Circumference = 2 pi r = 2 times (22/7) times 7 = 44 cm.

items.stem: Two angles lie on a straight line. If one of them is 110 degrees, what is the size of the other?
items.explanation: Angles on a straight line sum to 180 degrees, so the other angle is 180 - 110 = 70 degrees.

items.stem: In a right-angled triangle the two shorter sides are 3 cm and 4 cm. Find the length of the hypotenuse.
items.explanation: By the theorem of Pythagoras the hypotenuse squared is 3^2 + 4^2 = 9 + 16 = 25, so the hypotenuse is 5 cm.

items.stem: What is the value of sin 30 degrees?
items.explanation: From the standard special angles, sin 30 degrees equals one half, or 0.5, a value worth memorising.

items.stem: What is the value of cos 60 degrees?
items.explanation: From the standard special angles, cos 60 degrees equals one half, or 0.5.

items.stem: What is the value of tan 45 degrees?
items.explanation: At 45 degrees the opposite and adjacent sides are equal, so tan 45 = 1 because sine and cosine are equal there.

items.stem: In a right-angled triangle the side opposite an angle is 3 cm and the hypotenuse is 5 cm. What is the sine of that angle?
items.explanation: Sine is opposite over hypotenuse, so the value is 3 divided by 5 = 0.6.

items.stem: A vertical pole 1.5 m tall casts a shadow 1.5 m long on level ground. What is the angle of elevation of the sun?
items.explanation: The tangent of the angle is height over shadow, which is 1.5 divided by 1.5 = 1, and tan 45 degrees = 1, so the angle is 45 degrees.

items.stem: Find the distance between the points (0, 0) and (3, 4) on the Cartesian plane.
items.explanation: Using the distance formula, the distance is the square root of (3^2 + 4^2) = the square root of 25 = 5.

items.stem: Find the coordinates of the midpoint of the points (2, 4) and (6, 8).
items.explanation: The midpoint averages the coordinates, giving ((2 + 6)/2, (4 + 8)/2) = (4, 6).

items.stem: Find the gradient of the straight line passing through the points (1, 2) and (3, 8).
items.explanation: Gradient is the change in y divided by the change in x, which is (8 - 2)/(3 - 1) = 6/2 = 3.

items.stem: Find the equation of the straight line with gradient 2 that passes through the point (0, 3).
items.explanation: The line cuts the y axis at 3, so the intercept is 3, and the equation is y = 2x + 3.

items.stem: Find the volume of a cube whose edge is 4 cm long.
items.explanation: The volume of a cube is the edge cubed, so it is 4 times 4 times 4 = 64 cubic cm.

items.stem: Which of the following is the SI unit of force?
items.explanation: Force is measured in newtons; the joule measures energy, the watt measures power and the pascal measures pressure.

items.stem: A car travels a distance of 120 km in 2 hours. What is its average speed?
items.explanation: Average speed is distance divided by time, so it is 120 km divided by 2 h = 60 km per hour.

items.stem: What is the approximate value of the acceleration due to gravity near the surface of the earth?
items.explanation: The acceleration due to gravity is approximately 9.8 metres per second squared, often rounded to 10 in simple calculations.

items.stem: Which instrument is used to measure atmospheric pressure?
items.explanation: A barometer measures atmospheric pressure; a thermometer measures temperature, a hygrometer measures humidity and an ammeter measures current.

items.stem: What kind of energy does a moving body possess?
items.explanation: A body in motion possesses kinetic energy, while potential energy is stored, chemical energy is in substances and nuclear energy is in atomic nuclei.

items.stem: In a circuit a resistor of 4 ohms carries a current when the potential difference across it is 12 volts. Find the current.
items.explanation: By the law of Ohm, current is voltage divided by resistance, so I = 12 divided by 4 = 3 amperes.

items.stem: What is the SI unit of electric current?
items.explanation: Electric current is measured in amperes; the volt measures potential difference, the ohm resistance and the coulomb charge.

items.stem: Through which of the following media does light travel fastest?
items.explanation: Light travels fastest in a vacuum because there are no particles to slow it down; it is slower in air, water and glass.

items.stem: Which of the following can sound waves not travel through?
items.explanation: Sound needs a material medium, so it cannot travel through a vacuum; it travels through solids, liquids and gases.

items.stem: What is the main purpose of a simple machine such as a lever?
options: To make work easier by multiplying force
To increase the total amount of work done
items.explanation: A simple machine makes work easier, often by multiplying the applied force or changing its direction, but it cannot increase the total work done.

items.stem: A solid has a mass of 20 g and a volume of 4 cubic cm. Calculate its density.
items.explanation: Density is mass divided by volume, so it is 20 divided by 4 = 5 g per cubic cm.

items.stem: A force of 10 N moves an object through a distance of 3 m. Calculate the work done.
items.explanation: Work done is force multiplied by distance, so it is 10 times 3 = 30 joules.

items.stem: A machine does 60 J of work in 3 seconds. Calculate its power.
items.explanation: Power is work divided by time, so it is 60 divided by 3 = 20 watts.

items.stem: What is the bending of light as it passes from one transparent medium into another called?
items.explanation: Refraction is the change of direction of light as it passes between media of different densities; reflection bounces it back and diffraction spreads it around edges.

items.stem: Which device converts electrical energy into mechanical energy?
items.explanation: An electric motor converts electrical energy into motion; a generator does the opposite, a transformer changes voltage and a battery stores chemical energy.

items.stem: What is the chemical symbol for sodium?
items.explanation: Sodium has the symbol Na, from its Latin name natrium; N is the symbol for nitrogen, and So and Sd are not real symbols.

items.stem: What is the chemical formula of water?
items.explanation: Water is made of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom, giving the formula H2O; H2O2 is hydrogen peroxide.

items.stem: What is the atomic number of carbon?
items.explanation: Carbon has six protons in its nucleus, so its atomic number is 6; the number 12 is its common mass number.

items.stem: What is the pH value of a neutral aqueous solution at room temperature?
items.explanation: A neutral solution has a pH of 7; values below 7 are acidic and values above 7 are alkaline.

items.stem: Which gas is produced when a reactive metal reacts with a dilute acid?
items.explanation: A reactive metal displaces hydrogen from a dilute acid, so hydrogen gas is released, and it burns with a pop.

items.stem: Which gas makes up the largest proportion of the air we breathe?
items.explanation: Nitrogen makes up about 78 percent of air, oxygen about 21 percent, and carbon dioxide only a small fraction.

items.stem: What is the change of a solid directly into a gas without passing through the liquid state called?
items.explanation: Sublimation is the direct change from solid to gas, as when dry ice or camphor vapourises; the other terms describe different changes of state.

items.stem: Which of the following is the simplest member of the alkane family of organic compounds?
items.explanation: Methane, CH4, has a single carbon atom and is the simplest alkane; ethane, propane and butane have two, three and four carbons respectively.

items.stem: Which functional group is present in all alcohols?
items.explanation: Alcohols all contain the hydroxyl group OH; the carboxyl group is found in acids and the amino group in amines.

items.stem: What is the chemical formula of common table salt?
items.explanation: Table salt is sodium chloride, NaCl; KCl is potassium chloride and Na2CO3 is washing soda.

items.stem: What is the reaction between an acid and a base to form a salt and water called?
items.explanation: An acid reacting with a base to form a salt and water is neutralisation; oxidation and reduction involve electron changes and fermentation involves microorganisms.

items.stem: Rusting of iron requires oxygen and one other substance. What is that substance?
items.explanation: Iron rusts when it is exposed to both oxygen and moisture, so water is required; nitrogen and carbon dioxide do not cause rusting.

items.stem: How many electrons are there in a neutral oxygen atom, whose atomic number is 8?
items.explanation: A neutral atom has as many electrons as protons, and the atomic number gives the proton count, so oxygen has 8 electrons.

items.stem: Which method is used to separate a mixture of sand and water?
items.explanation: Filtration separates an insoluble solid like sand from a liquid, while distillation and evaporation are used for dissolved substances.

items.stem: What is the process by which green plants manufacture their own food called?
items.explanation: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants use sunlight, carbon dioxide and water to make food; respiration releases energy instead.

items.stem: What is the basic structural and functional unit of all living things?
items.explanation: The cell is the basic unit of life; tissues, organs and whole organisms are built from cells.

items.stem: Which organ of the human body pumps blood to all parts of the body?
items.explanation: The heart is a muscular pump that circulates blood; the liver, lungs and kidneys perform other essential functions.

items.stem: Which gas is taken in by humans during respiration?
items.explanation: Humans take in oxygen during respiration and give out carbon dioxide; nitrogen is not used in respiration.

items.stem: Which gas is released by green plants into the atmosphere during photosynthesis?
items.explanation: During photosynthesis plants take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen; carbon dioxide is the gas they absorb, not release.

items.stem: In which part of the human body does the digestion of food begin?
items.explanation: Digestion begins in the mouth, where teeth break down food and saliva starts the breakdown of starch.

items.stem: What name is given to all the organisms of the same species living together in one area?
items.explanation: A population is a group of individuals of the same species in an area; a community includes different species and an ecosystem includes the physical environment.

items.stem: From which source does the flow of energy in most ecosystems originally begin?
items.explanation: Energy in ecosystems begins with the sun, which green plants capture and pass on to other organisms through food chains.

items.stem: What name is given to organisms that break down dead plants and animals and release nutrients?
items.explanation: Decomposers such as bacteria and fungi break down dead matter and return nutrients to the soil; producers make food and herbivores eat plants.

items.stem: Which green pigment in plants traps light energy for photosynthesis?
items.explanation: Chlorophyll is the green pigment that absorbs light for photosynthesis; haemoglobin carries oxygen in blood and melanin colours skin.

items.stem: Which type of blood cell defends the human body against infection?
items.explanation: White blood cells fight infection by engulfing germs and producing antibodies; red blood cells carry oxygen and platelets help blood to clot.
